hook.content: Imagine you are a detective in letter-land! Every time you open your mouth to talk, you are actually making secret code sounds that build words. Today, we are going to unlock the secret sounds for four very special letters: m, s, a, and t!

bigIdea.statement: Letters are like magic symbols that make specific sounds, and when we put those sounds together, we can build whole words!
bigIdea.whyItMatters: Knowing letter sounds is the superpower that unlocks reading, helping you read your favorite books all by yourself.

curatorBrief.title: Welcome to the Sound Safari: Letters m, s, a, t!
curatorBrief.intent: Hook early learners with an engaging introduction to the sounds made by the letters m, s, a, and t. Introduce the two essential goals: hearing and saying each sound out loud, and connecting each spoken sound to its printed letter shape.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Hear and say the individual sounds for the letters m, s, a, and t

components.title: Meet the Four Special Sounds
components.intent: Introduce the four target phonemes (/m/, /s/, /æ/, /t/) using child-friendly keywords and vivid picture anchors: humming /m/ with a smiling face eating a treat ('mmm'), hissing /s/ with a slithering snake ('sss'), crisp short /a/ with an apple ('ah'), and ticking /t/ with a clock or tennis ball ('t-t-t').

components.title: Listen and Say the Sounds
components.intent: Provide Direct Instruction oral practice where the tutor models each continuous sound (/m/, /s/, /a/) and prompts the student to say the target sound into the microphone with supportive auditory guidance and instant affirmation.

components.title: Sound Detective: Match Beginning Sounds
components.intent: Challenge students to hear words starting with /m/, /s/, /a/, and /t/ and speak the matching word or sound aloud, reinforcing auditory discrimination across all four phonemes.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Identify the printed letters m, s, a, and t that match the sounds

components.title: Find the Letters: m, s, a, t
components.intent: Direct Instruction letter recognition game where the tutor prompts students to identify and tap the printed graphemes m, s, a, and t among visual choices, building visual letter discrimination.

components.title: Link the Sound to the Letter
components.intent: Connect the hearing of the sound directly to selecting its printed letter form. The tutor prompts with a target sound (/m/, /s/, /a/, /t/) and students tap or speak the correct matching printed letter.

components.title: Trace and Build m, s, a, t
components.intent: Reinforce grapheme identification kinesthetically by tracing the strokes of lowercase letters m, s, a, and t with gentle stroke guides.

finalAssessment.title: Super Sound and Letter Master Challenge
finalAssessment.intent: Assess mastery of both learning objectives together: prompt students to identify spoken initial sounds for m, s, a, t, and match spoken sounds to their correct printed letters.

problems.question: Which one starts with the ssss sound?
problems.rationale: Sun starts with the /s/ sound, just like a hissing snake: sss-un! Apple begins with the short /a/ sound, and mat begins with the /m/ sound. Listening carefully to the very first sound helps us match words to their letter sounds.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to stretch out the first sound with a physical gesture, such as making a slithering snake motion with their arm while making the /s/ sound.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /s/ sound in spoken words
Distinguish the initial /s/ sound from /a/ and /m/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the same sound as tiger?
problems.rationale: Tiger and tent both start with the /t/ sound. When you say tiger and tent, your tongue taps the top of your mouth at the start. Apple and ant begin with the /a/ sound instead.
problems.teachingNote: Have students isolate the initial sound by tapping their chin or shoulder as they say /t/-iger and /t/-ent. Point out how the mouth forms the /t/ burst compared to the open mouth for /a/.
successCriteria: Identify words that begin with the /t/ sound.
Distinguish between the beginning sounds /t/ and /a/.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the letter M sound?
problems.rationale: Moon begins with the /m/ sound made by the letter M. Star begins with the /s/ sound, and ant begins with the short /a/ sound.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to press their lips together to feel the humming /m/ sound when saying moon.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /m/ sound in familiar spoken words.
Differentiate the letter M sound from other consonant and vowel sounds.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the mmmm sound?
problems.rationale: Monkey begins with the letter M, which makes the /m/ sound. Turtle begins with the /t/ sound, and apple begins with the /a/ sound.
problems.teachingNote: Have children press their lips together to feel the vibration when making the /m/ sound, comparing it to the quick tongue tap of /t/.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /m/ sound in spoken words.
